pages.title: A walk to the museum in Boston · 1/3
paragraphs: On my second day in Boston, I wanted to see a museum. I was near a park, and I saw a woman with a coffee. “**Excuse me, how do I get to the museum?**” I asked.
“**Go straight for two blocks**,” she said. I repeated, “Two blocks, then?” She smiled. “**Turn left at the traffic light**.” “And then?” I asked. “**Walk one more block. It’s on your right**.”
pages.prompt: Onde começa e o que acontece?

pages.title: A walk to the museum in Boston · 2/3
paragraphs: I asked, “Is it a big building?” “**Yes, with a red door**,” she said. “**Good luck! You can’t miss it**.” I said thanks and started to walk. The sun was warm, and the streets were quiet.
I counted: one block, two blocks. At the corner, there was a traffic light, and it was red. I waited. When it turned green, I crossed and turned left. I walked one more block and looked to my right.

pages.title: A walk to the museum in Boston · 3/3
paragraphs: There it was! A tall brick building with a big red door. The woman was right: I could not miss it. I felt proud because I understood the directions in English.
Next time, I will ask more questions and use my phone less. People are friendly, and a short conversation can be the best map.

pages.title: Dar o caminho
pages.frame: Go straight for {n} blocks. {act} at the {mark}.
pages.model: Go straight for two blocks. Turn left at the traffic light.
pages.note: Fale em passos curtos: uma instrução por frase.

pages.title: Som e ritmo
pairs: O “n” de “turn” e o “l” de “left” ficam juntos. “At the” é fraco e rápido.
Marque “go”, “straight” e “blocks”. As outras palavras são curtas.
“Can’t” soa forte e longo; “can” afirmativo é fraco. Aqui a voz cai em “miss”.
